articles.author: Will Bloom

articles.title: South Africa’s ANC Is Collapsing. The Far Right Is Rising.
articles.author: Zwelinzima Vavi
articles.content_excerpt: While the global left celebrates the recent successes of the Workers’ Party in Brazil and the Democratic Socialists of America in the United States, the African National Congress (ANC) has suffered a historic collapse in South Africa’s November 4 local government elections. After three decades of mass unemployment, deepening inequality, corruption, and economic policies that have failed the working class, the former liberation movement is losing its political authority. The principal beneficiaries of the ANC’s electoral rout are parties of the Right, including an increasingly powerful far right that has built its project around aggressive and often violent xenophobia. articles.author: Eileen Jones
articles.content_excerpt: There’s a familiar but always thrilling moment in Godzilla Minus Zero when Godzilla is fighting the newer, faster, entirely more visually glamorous monster King Ghidorah — an immense three-headed, golden-ray-shooting dragon that seems set on destroying the human race — and Godzilla is losing. In fact, it seems Godzilla is beaten and dying. But then Godzilla goes deep and dredges up the last of his prehistoric mojo and comes back to win the brutal kaiju battle. Godzilla the destroyer from the sea becomes Godzilla the hero and savior of the Japanese protagonists watching in wide-eyed terror. All the viewer’s childhood love of Godzilla, who lumbers around on big, squat feet like a crude, clumsy dinosaur based on some devoted but impractical kid’s drawing, surges to the fore. articles.title: Under Capitalism, Even Kids’ Playtime Is Alienated
articles.author: Evelina Johansson Wilén
articles.content_excerpt: A central concern of feminist Marxist theory and practice has been how to understand the relationship between paid and unpaid labor. Marxist feminists have drawn on Karl Marx’s observation that capital leaves workers to ensure their own reproduction, a process that depends on their instinct for self-preservation. They have shown how capitalist accumulation depends on reproductive labor, work that has fallen primarily to women. But what, exactly, is being reproduced? Workers must replenish their strength so that they can work again the next day; importantly, reproduction also encompasses bearing children and creating future labor power. articles.title: France’s “Hot Autumn” Is Boosting the Left
articles.author: Stathis Kouvelakis
articles.content_excerpt: Since mid-September, a wave of protest has swept across France. High school students in working-class banlieues (suburbs) and the overseas territories started it by occupying their schools. University students, teachers, trade unionists, and a new generation of yellow vests ( gilets jaunes ) soon joined them. On November 5, about 1.6 million people took to the streets in two hundred cities. Emmanuel Macron’s government has answered with the harshest crackdown in half a century. Police have arrested more than ten thousand people, most of them teenagers. A new “Rioters Pay” bill would punish protesters for acts they did not personally commit. articles.title: Economics News for Workers, November 2026
articles.content_excerpt: A Gallup poll on the eve of the election measured the issues of most salience to American voters. Unsurprisingly, the state of the economy was considered the most important, with 87 percent rating it either extremely or very important.
